title: The Electron in the W-Structure: Spin, Magnetic Moment, Charge and Motion
description: In the W-Structure, space is points that never rest: every point exchanges places with a neighbour at every tick, and one exchange is one step and one tick. A particle is a stable pattern of exchanges that moves along its own closed path. The work traces what the author's positions imply for the electron and labels every statement by its status. A circulation at c with radius ħ/(mc) gives the magnetic moment μ_B; with spin ħ/2 from the rule 'orientation returns after two cycles', g = 2, while the circulation itself carries ħ — an open contradiction. If the loops of a charged particle lie in the plane of its circulation, charge is the only sign invariant under rotations and reflection and odd under loop reversal; the loops of a neutrino cannot lie in its circulation plane. Places without a lattice are isotropic on average, and in one realization the fluctuations of the propagation speed fall with distance as expected for first passage in three dimensions. A clock moving in its own plane keeps the period γ only if contracted by γ; full Lorentz invariance is a candidate under a stated premise. Hydrogen as Kepler loops with a whole number of wavelengths gives the levels and the 1s momentum distribution, but the electron density at the proton is wrong, so the ensemble is excluded by the 21 cm line. Mass is defined by closures per own tick of a particle; the mass of a composite system is not yet defined. Programs reproduce every computed number. Open problems are listed.
